solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poor side in cricket going about brand new game

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: poor in quality means bad
the on side is one half of a cricket field (also called leg side)
something in mint condition is brand new

explanation.surface: A weak cricket team gets a fresh sporting outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going about' has the poor side wrap around the brand-new piece. In cricket the field divides into the off side and the on side, the latter also called leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Sculpture in pieces

definitions.meaning: a carved head and shoulders on a plinth
broken, as in a gadget that has gone kaput

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a carved head-and-shoulders piece, and the informal adjective for broken.

clue.text: Failure to inspire a couple of learners, a right dunce!

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the outer word takes the others inside it

parts.note: a dud is something that fails to work
L is the learner-driver abbreviation, and two of them make LL

explanation.surface: A teacher despairs that a pair of pupils, one a real dunce, cannot be motivated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failure to inspire' reads as one phrase, but 'Failure' is DUD and 'to inspire' signals it breathing in LL, A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A dullard is a slow-witted person, a synonym of dunce.

clue.text: Fury, as father blows top

indicators.note: the word loses its top letter, the first one in a down light

parts.note: to sire is to father, and a sire is a male parent

explanation.surface: Dad loses his temper in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows top' is also an idiom for losing one's temper, which fits 'Fury'; here it removes the S of SIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary word for anger, a synonym of fury.

clue.text: The military display a particular image on arms?

definitions.meaning: a military ... is an evening display of drumming and marching, like the Edinburgh one
an inked design on the skin, often on the arms

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an outdoor military pageant and a permanent inked picture on the skin; 'arms' teases weapons.

clue.text: A must to build city with sense

indicators.note: building assembles the letters into a new structure

explanation.surface: Building a city sensibly is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to build' rearranges CITY and SENSE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is a must is required, an essential requirement.

clue.text: Donkey covered in molasses

indicators.note: the letters sit covered by the surrounding word

explanation.surface: A donkey smeared with treacle.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is the animal, a synonym of donkey.

clue.text: Guardian article set

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
to gel is to set, as jelly does

explanation.surface: A piece in the Guardian newspaper is ready to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper but is the definition, as in guardian angel.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian angel is a protecting spirit, so a guardian can be called an angel.

clue.text: Unexpected present, old instrument

indicators.note: an unexpected arrangement of the letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A surprise gift turns out to be an antique musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The serpent is an obsolete bass wind instrument with a snaking shape.

clue.text: A silent suspect, conspicuous

indicators.note: suspect letters are doubtful, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suspect who stays quiet stands out.
explanation.definitionFit: A salient feature is the most noticeable one, a synonym of prominent.

clue.text: Smoke in garage starts to fill vehicle

indicators.note: the picked letters fill the middle of the other word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: the starts of two words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Fumes in a garage fill a parked car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes I and G from 'in garage', and 'to fill' puts them inside CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigar is something one smokes, and 'a smoke' is informal for a cigar or cigarette.

clue.text: Young lady produced wine, I gathered

parts.note: made means produced

indicators.note: the wine gathers the letter in, holding it inside

parts.note: Moselle is a German white wine from the Mosel valley

explanation.surface: A winemaker reports on a vintage brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' reads like harvesting grapes, but it signals the wine taking the I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The French title for an unmarried woman, used in English for a young woman or girl.

clue.text: Former remits corrected, having little time for zealot

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former

indicators.note: corrected letters are put into a new order

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, a little version of the word

explanation.surface: Revised terms of reference leave a fanatic short of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrected' rearranges the letters of 'remits' (TREMIS); 'having' just joins on the T. 'remits' looks like a noun, terms of reference, but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremist holds fanatical views, which is what a zealot does.

clue.text: Untidy, muddled exposure

indicators.note: muddled letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Scruffy and confused, someone has been caught exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudity is being unclothed, a form of indecent exposure.

clue.text: Anaesthetists in OT book?

definitions.meaning: people who deaden feeling, read playfully as those who make things numb
the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Anaesthetists at work in the operating theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: OT in the surface suggests operating theatre; it is the Old Testament. 'Anaesthetists' is read as numb-ers, people who numb.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaesthetist numbs patients, so playfully is a numb-er; the Old Testament's fourth book has the same name.

clue.text: Idiot in retired nincompoop

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the short word is read backwards

parts.note: a twit is a fool, a nincompoop

explanation.surface: An idiot among retired fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns IN into NI, followed by TWIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a silly person, a synonym of idiot.

clue.text: Vehicle's driver departed during conflict

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, as an event within a period

parts.note: a war is a conflict
gone means departed

explanation.surface: A driver left in the middle of a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' reads as time, but it signals placing one piece inside the other; 'Vehicle's driver' is the definition, not a possessive in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagoner drives a wagon, a horse-drawn vehicle.

clue.text: A piece of poetry that's unsympathetic

parts.note: a verse is a piece of poetry

explanation.surface: A poem that shows no compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Averse means opposed or hostile to something, hence not sympathetic towards it.

clue.text: Any video game is unintelligible first time out

indicators.note: unintelligible letters make no sense as they are and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A gamer finds a new video game baffling on first play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unintelligible' rearranges all of ANY VIDEO GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's first voyage is its maiden one, so the phrase means a first outing.

clue.text: White substance that's key?

definitions.meaning: the creamy material of elephant tusks
piano keys were traditionally made of this tusk material, so a key is informally one of the ivories

explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is white tusk material, and 'tickling the ivories' means playing piano keys.

clue.text: Canteen in awful state

explanation.definitionFit: A mess is both a service dining room and a state of chaotic disorder.

clue.text: Harmful thing, priest inhaling carbon monoxide

indicators.note: breathing in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel
CO is the chemical formula for carbon monoxide

explanation.surface: A priest is poisoned by breathing in carbon monoxide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inhaling' signals one piece taken inside the other. Eli, the priest who raised Samuel, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: E. coli is a bacterium whose toxic strains cause food poisoning, a harmful thing.

clue.text: Train entire cast to captivate you, finally

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so the rearranged letters hold the pick inside
cast letters are thrown into a new arrangement
the final letter of the word is the pick

explanation.surface: A director rehearses the whole cast to enchant the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges ENTIRE to RETINE; 'to captivate' takes in U, the last letter of 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the train of attendants following an important person.

clue.text: Earl Grey? A character, they say?

indicators.note: what people say out loud is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a character is a letter, here the letter T

explanation.surface: Is Earl Grey, the aristocrat, quite a character?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earl Grey' looks like a nobleman; it is the bergamot-flavoured tea named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl Grey is a blend flavoured with bergamot, an example of the drink, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Give voice, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to utter or express in words
used like 'for example' to introduce a possibility

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to utter, and the word also introduces an example, like 'for instance'.

clue.text: Reference the tail of an old reptile?

parts.note: many dinosaur names end in -saurus, as in brontosaurus, so it is the tail end of such a name

explanation.surface: Pointing to the tail of a dinosaur fossil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail' is the ending of a dinosaur's name, not its physical tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book listing synonyms.
